sections.h2: What does the Montgomery County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
The Montgomery County Register of Deeds records deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and releases for land in the county, and keeps the index that lets anyone trace who has owned a parcel. The county describes the office on its department page as the legal custodian of the real estate and vital records for Montgomery County.

The same office records military discharge papers (DD 214), assumed name and partnership filings, and UCC fixture filings. It also issues marriage licenses and certified copies of birth, death and marriage records, and it swears in notaries commissioned in the county.

For a homeowner planning a sale, the land records side is the part that counts. Every deed you sign and every mortgage payoff that clears your title ends up in these books. A buyer's title search in Troy, Biscoe, Candor, Star or Mount Gilead runs through this one index, so the office sits at the end of every Montgomery County closing, including a quick cash sale.

sections.h2: How big is Montgomery County, and what does that mean for selling a house here?
sections.html:
Montgomery County is a small, rural county in the Uwharrie region with 26,403 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. It covers 491.54 square miles of land, so the population density works out to 52.4 people per square mile in the 2020 count.

That low density shapes how houses trade. Buyers often commute, and the Census puts the average trip to work at 27.1 minutes. The median home value in the table below is a useful yardstick when you weigh a repair bill against a sale price.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax when a Montgomery County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. North Carolina law makes the transferor pay the excise tax to the register of deeds of the county where the land lies before the deed can be recorded (G.S. 105-228.30).

The statute sets the rate at one dollar on each five hundred dollars, or fractional part of that, of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed. The county keeps one half of the receipts in its general fund and the other half goes to the State through the Department of Revenue.

  • The tax is collected at the Montgomery County office when the deed is presented, so your closing attorney usually brings a check or arranges payment ahead of time.
  • A parcel that straddles two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value.
  • The amount is stated on the face of the recorded deed, so a buyer, lender or later researcher can read it from the public record.

Ask the closing attorney for the exact figure before you sign, because it depends on the price or value that goes on the deed.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed or mortgage in Montgomery County?
sections.html:
Recording fees are the same in every North Carolina county because the legislature fixed them in G.S. 161-10. The statute calls the fees complete and exclusive and says they are collected before a document is filed.

  • General instruments, including most deeds: $26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each extra page.
  • Deeds of trust and mortgages: $64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 for each extra page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of a deed of trust or mortgage: no fee.
  • Plats: $21.00 per sheet.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each additional page.
  • Non-standard document add-on: $25.00.

The free satisfaction is worth knowing about if you are paying off a loan with sale proceeds. The lender files it, and your title stays clean at no charge to you.

sections.h2: How do Montgomery County property taxes connect to the recorded deed?
sections.html:
The county's Tax Administrator keeps the ownership and parcel records that start from what the register of deeds records, then bills and collects the tax. The county tax department page says the office handles about 30,000 parcels of real property.

Who sends your bill depends on where the house sits. The county collects its own tax and the real estate tax for four of its five towns: Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead. Troy collects its own. Three fire districts are billed with the county bill: Lake Tillery, Badin Lake and Wadeville.

  • Taxes are due September 1, and the county says they are not past due until January 5.
  • Listing season for personal property runs January 2 to January 31, with a 10% late listing penalty after that.
  • The county was last revalued in 2020, and its next reappraisal is scheduled for 2028.
  • The commissioners set the rate each June, and bills go out in July and August.

The tax lien on a parcel attaches as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, and unpaid taxes can lead to foreclosure on the house. If the closing is near the end of the year, ask the tax office or the town for a payoff figure so the bill is settled at the table.

sections.h2: What happens if a Montgomery County deed is signed but never recorded?
sections.html:
An unrecorded deed does not protect the buyer against outsiders. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, or lease running longer than three years is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value except from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies.

Priority follows the order and time of registration. If a seller signs a deed, then a creditor files a judgment before the deed is recorded, the creditor may come first. For heirs who have been holding a signed deed in a drawer for years, that gap is a real risk.

The fix is simple. Take the signed, acknowledged deed to the office, pay the excise tax and recording fee, and keep the recording information the office returns to you.

sections.h2: What should a Montgomery County seller line up before recording?
sections.html:
Most of the work happens before anyone walks into the office. A closing attorney normally prepares the deed, since register of deeds staff in North Carolina do not draft documents or give legal advice.

  • Pull the parcel number and ownership record from the county's real estate and GIS search so the legal description on the deed matches the tax record.
  • Collect payoff letters for any mortgage or lien, and confirm the lender will file its satisfaction.
  • Confirm who collects the tax on the parcel: the county or the Town of Troy.
  • Have the excise tax and recording fee ready as separate amounts.
  • Keep the notarized original and the recording stamp together once the deed is filed.

Ask the Montgomery County Register of Deeds directly for current office hours and the ways the office accepts documents, since those can change.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The transferor pays the tax to the Montgomery County Register of Deeds before the deed is recorded, at one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value or fraction of that amount, per G.S. 105-228.30.

faqs.q: What does the Montgomery County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A general instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each additional page, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 per extra page. These statewide fees come from G.S. 161-10, and satisfactions of a deed of trust carry no fee.

faqs.q: Can the register of deeds write my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. North Carolina register of deeds offices record documents but cannot prepare them or give legal advice, so a closing attorney or other lawyer drafts the deed. The office then records it once it is signed and notarized.

faqs.q: When are Montgomery County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1 each year, and the county says they are not past due until January 5. State law adds 2% interest from January 6 and three-fourths of one percent a month starting February 1.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a house inside the Town of Troy?
faqs.a: The Town of Troy collects its own real estate tax. The county tax office collects the county bill and the bills for Biscoe, Star, Candor and Mount Gilead, so a Troy owner may receive separate county and town bills.
